paragraphs.title: An Invitation to the Source of Life and Abundance

easy.explanation: The verse begins, “Ho, every one that thirsteth, come ye to the waters.”
easy.q: Who is invited to come to the waters?

easy.explanation: The verse invites people to buy “wine and milk without money and without price.”
easy.q: What may be bought without money and without price?

answers: Hearken and hear unto the Lord
easy.explanation: The passage says, “Incline your ear, and come unto me: hear, and your soul shall live.”
easy.q: What should the people do so that their souls may live?

answers: Because the Lord gives what is good and truly satisfies
Because money belongs only to kings
medium.explanation: The passage contrasts labor that does not satisfy with hearing God and eating that which is good.
medium.q: Why are the people told to hearken unto the Lord instead of spending money for that which satisfieth not?

answers: To obtain or receive what is offered
medium.explanation: The invitation concerns receiving food and drink freely, without money or price.
medium.q: In the phrase “come ye, buy,” what does “buy” mean in context?

answers: As a witness, leader, and commander
As someone separated from all nations
medium.explanation: The Lord says, “I have given him for a witness to the people, a leader and commander to the people.”
medium.q: How is David described in relation to the people?

answers: They are connected with receiving life and true good
challenge.explanation: The passage presents coming to God as the way to receive satisfaction, goodness, and life for the soul.
challenge.q: What idea is shared by the waters, food, and hearing the Lord?

answers: Because the Lord has glorified Israel
challenge.explanation: The nations will run unto Israel “because of the Lord thy God... for he hath glorified thee.”
challenge.q: Why will nations run unto Israel?

answers: An invitation to receive good, a call to hear God, and a mission to the nations
Labor, wealth, and building a temple
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from free provision to hearing God and then to Israel’s witness and leadership among the nations.
challenge.q: Which sequence of ideas appears in verses 1–5?

paragraphs.title: A Call to Seek God and Return While He Is Near

easy.explanation: The verse says, “Seek ye the Lord.”
easy.q: Whom are the people called to seek?

answers: When no one is in the city
easy.explanation: The verse says, “call ye upon him while he is near.”
easy.q: When are the people told to call upon the Lord?

answers: Forsake his way and return unto the Lord
easy.explanation: The wicked are told to forsake their way and return unto the Lord.
easy.q: What should the wicked person do?

medium.explanation: The Lord will have mercy, and God will “abundantly pardon.”
medium.q: What will a person receive when he returns unto the Lord?

answers: A person who is morally wrong or wicked
medium.explanation: The verse calls the person to forsake his unrighteous thoughts and return to God.
medium.q: In the phrase “the unrighteous man his thoughts,” what does “unrighteous” describe?

answers: Because this is the time to call upon Him and return
Because no change is then required
Because people can safely turn away from Him
medium.explanation: The verse joins seeking the Lord with calling upon Him while He is near.
medium.q: Why is it important to seek the Lord while he may be found?

answers: Forsaking evil thoughts as well as an evil way
challenge.explanation: The passage requires the wicked to forsake both his way and his thoughts.
challenge.q: What inward change is required, not merely an outward change?

challenge.explanation: The verse declares that God will “abundantly pardon.”

answers: True seeking of the Lord includes repentance
Seeking the Lord requires continuing in wickedness
challenge.explanation: The verses place seeking God alongside forsaking sinful ways and thoughts and returning to Him.
challenge.q: What is the connection between seeking the Lord and forsaking wickedness?

paragraphs.title: The Supremacy of God’s Ways and the Power of His Word

answers: They are higher than human thoughts
They are lower than human thoughts
easy.explanation: The Lord says, “my thoughts are not your thoughts,” and that His thoughts are higher.
easy.q: How are the Lord’s thoughts compared with human thoughts?

answers: It waters the earth and helps it produce
It covers the earth with stones
easy.explanation: The rain waters the earth and makes it bring forth and bud.
easy.q: What does rain do to the earth?

answers: It does not return unto Him void
It does not go forth from His mouth
easy.explanation: The verse says, “it shall not return unto me void.”
easy.q: What does the Lord’s word not do?

answers: As rain works upon the earth, God’s word accomplishes its purpose
medium.explanation: Rain produces growth, just as God’s word accomplishes what He pleases.
medium.q: What does the rain illustrate about the word of God?

answers: God’s word will not return without accomplishing its purpose
God’s word never leaves His mouth
God’s word returns without any change
medium.explanation: The next phrase explains that God’s word accomplishes what He pleases and prospers in its mission.
medium.q: What does “it shall not return unto me void” mean?

answers: Rain enables growth that provides seed and bread
medium.explanation: The rain waters the earth so that it gives seed to the sower and bread to the eater.
medium.q: What is the connection between rain, seed, and bread?

answers: God’s ways cannot be measured by human understanding alone
Human ways are higher than God’s ways
There is no difference between God’s ways and human ways
challenge.explanation: The great height of the heavens above the earth illustrates the greatness of the difference between God’s ways and ours.
challenge.q: What conclusion follows from the comparison between the heavens and the earth and between God’s ways and human ways?

answers: It accomplishes what God pleases and prospers in the thing whereunto He sends it
It falls from heaven as rain
challenge.explanation: The verse describes God’s word as accomplishing His purpose and prospering in its assignment.
challenge.q: What shows that God’s word acts with a definite purpose?

answers: Though people have sinned, God makes a way for them to return and receive pardon
God shows mercy only to those who have never sinned
challenge.explanation: The surrounding passage joins God’s higher ways with His willingness to forgive those who return to Him.
challenge.q: How do God’s mercy and the supremacy of His ways fit together?

paragraphs.title: The Joy of Redemption and the Renewal of the World

easy.explanation: The verse says, “ye shall go out with joy.”
easy.q: How will the people go out?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “be led forth with peace.”
easy.q: How will the people be led forth?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “Instead of the thorn shall come up the fir tree.”
easy.q: What tree will come up instead of the thorn?

medium.explanation: The mountains and hills “shall break forth before you into singing.”
medium.q: How do the mountains and hills participate in redemption?

answers: To burst out in joyful song
medium.explanation: The phrase pictures the mountains and hills bursting out in joyful singing.
medium.q: What does “break forth” mean in the phrase “break forth into singing”?

answers: Renewal and the transformation of a barren place
medium.explanation: Useful and beautiful trees replace plants associated with barrenness and thorns.
medium.q: What do the changes from thorn to fir tree and from brier to myrtle tree represent?

answers: Going out with joy, being led in peace, and seeing the world renewed
Going out to war, suffering destruction, and returning to poverty
Silence, delay, and the disappearance of nature
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from joyful departure to peaceful leading, nature’s song, and renewed vegetation.
challenge.q: What is the central sequence in the description of redemption?

answers: They clap their hands and join the celebration
challenge.explanation: The verse says, “all the trees of the field shall clap their hands.”
challenge.q: What part do the trees of the field play in the scene?

answers: It shall be to the Lord for a name and an everlasting sign
It shall hide the glory of God
It shall show that nothing changes
challenge.explanation: The renewed land will be “to the Lord for a name, for an everlasting sign.”
challenge.q: What is the purpose of the renewal described at the end?
